title: The God Who Sees
body: Hagar calls God “the God who sees me.” Even when she felt alone in the wilderness, God noticed her pain and spoke to her by name.
question: Where in your life do you feel unnoticed or alone?
prayer: God who sees me, help me believe that You notice my tears, my questions, and my story today.

title: The Lord My Shepherd
body: Calling God our Shepherd means He leads, protects, and provides, not from a distance but with personal care.
question: Where do you most need God’s guidance or protection right now?
prayer: Lord my Shepherd, lead me today and help me trust that Your care is enough for me.

title: The Lord Who Heals
body: God reveals Himself as the One who heals. Sometimes He heals bodies, and often He heals hearts, memories, and attitudes.
question: What part of your life feels wounded or in need of healing?
prayer: Lord who heals, touch the places in me that are hurting and bring Your wholeness and peace.

title: The Lord Our Peace
body: In the middle of fear and uncertainty, Gideon builds an altar to the Lord and calls Him “The Lord is Peace.” God’s presence is greater than your fear.
question: What situation in your life feels chaotic or fearful right now?
prayer: God of peace, meet me in my fear and let Your presence quiet my heart.

title: The Lord Our Provider
body: Abraham calls God “The Lord will provide” after God supplies a ram in place of Isaac. God sees needs before we even can and is faithful in His timing.
question: Where are you worried about not having enough—time, money, energy, or strength?
prayer: Lord my Provider, help me trust that You know what I need and that You will not abandon me.

title: The Lord Our Righteousness
body: God promises a righteous King whose righteousness covers His people. Our standing with God rests on Him, not on our performance.
question: Where are you tempted to base your worth on success, appearance, or spirituality?
prayer: Lord our righteousness, thank You that my standing with You is grounded in Jesus and not in my perfection.

title: The Lord Is Near
body: The Lord is near to all who call on Him in truth. He is not far off, waiting for you to get your life together before you approach Him.
question: What keeps you from talking honestly with God about what is really going on?
prayer: Lord, help me come to You honestly today and trust that You stay close even when I feel a mess.

title: The Lord My Rock
body: Calling God a Rock means He is steady when everything else shifts. You can stand on Him when circumstances feel unstable.
question: What has felt shaky or unstable recently—your schedule, relationships, or emotions?
prayer: God my Rock, steady my heart and help me remember that You do not change even when my world does.

title: The Lord My Light
body: God as Light means He reveals truth, exposes lies, and leads you safely through darkness. His light is stronger than any shadow.
question: Where do you feel confused, unsure, or in the dark about what to do next?
prayer: Lord my Light, shine on my path and help me see the next faithful step to take.

title: The Lord Who Is There
body: God names the restored city “The Lord is there,” pointing to His unshakable presence with His people. You never walk into a room alone; He is already there.
question: Which upcoming place or situation makes you nervous to walk into?
prayer: Lord who is there, remind me that You go ahead of me and stay with me wherever I go.
